# `Http`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Http — outbound HTTP client.

`get` / `post` / `request` are effects (Task Error HttpResponse). The
runtime (`ipe_runtime::http_client`) is the PARSE boundary: it validates
the URL, enforces the SSRF guard, body cap, timeout floor, and error
redaction. These records are transport DTOs carried to that boundary;
downstream code MUST NOT re-validate.

A response body past `IPE_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, or a redirect chain past its
`FollowRedirects` maximum, fails with a `LimitExceeded` error.

Dial rule: a URL with `\` anywhere, or `@` in its path or fragment, is
refused (its credentials could run into the host) — write `@` as `%40`.
An `@` in the query is allowed, but an error for that URL then withholds
the host.

Request TARGETS are the typed `Ipe.Url.Url`, not a raw `String` — at EVERY
entry point. The one-shot senders `get` / `post` take a `Url`; the primary
constructor `defaultRequest` and the retarget setter `withUrl` take an
already-sealed `Url` (parsed exactly once at `Url.fromString`) and narrow
its scheme to `http`/`https` at THIS API layer, returning `Err` on any
other scheme. The narrowing is fail-closed BY CONSTRUCTION: a
builder-assembled request whose scheme is not `http(s)` cannot be built,
so it is rejected even when the runtime SSRF guard is disabled in
development — the runtime scheme allowlist is defence-in-depth, never the
only line. `defaultRequestFromString` is the MARKED raw-string boundary:
it runs `Url.fromString` and returns `Result`, so a raw string is an
explicit parse-at-the-boundary, never a silent stringly default. There is
no unmarked `String` request-target path: a caller reaches `get` / `post`
only by first passing a raw string through `Url.fromString`, which validates
it and returns a `Result`.

`HttpMethod` is a closed ADT — make-invalid-states-unrepresentable for
HTTP verbs. `methodFromString` is the single typed parse boundary for
inbound method strings (e.g. parsed from a server request line);
`methodToString` recovers the canonical uppercase string for logging or
forwarding. Unknown verbs surface as `Nothing` at the parse boundary,
never as a silent default.

Every function here is kernel-backed (resolved by qualifier to a
`ipe_runtime::http_client` fn); the Ipê bodies below mirror that behaviour
for reading, but the AUTHORITATIVE scheme-narrowing implementation is the
runtime `narrow_http_scheme` the kernels call — the two cannot diverge
because the kernel path, not these bodies, is what lowers.

`parseQuery` is pure: trims a leading `?`, splits on `&`/`=`, decodes each
key and value under the form grammar (`+` is a space), first-key-wins, and
returns a `Dict String String`. A malformed escape or invalid UTF-8 refuses
the whole query with an `InvalidInput` error; more than 1024 pairs, with a
`LimitExceeded` error.

Builders (`defaultRequest` / `with*`) are pure Ipe. `withHeader`
cons-prepends `(k, v)` onto `req.headers`, so the most-recently-added
header is first in the list.

## `HttpMethod`

Closed set of HTTP methods.  Use constructors directly in client code;
use `methodFromString` only at inbound parse boundaries (e.g. routing
layers that receive a raw method string from the network).

## `RedirectPolicy`

Redirect behaviour for an outbound request.  `NoRedirects` prevents all
redirects; `FollowRedirects n` follows up to `n` hops (negative values are
clamped to 0 at the runtime boundary).  Replaces the coupled
`followRedirects : Bool` / `maxRedirects : Int` pair, making the
"don't follow but here's a max count" contradiction unrepresentable.

## `defaultRequest`

```ipe
defaultRequest : Url -> Result Error HttpRequest
```

`defaultRequest url` — the primary request constructor. Takes an
already-sealed typed `Url` (parsed once at `Url.fromString`), narrows its
scheme to `http`/`https` at this API layer, and carries the single
canonical serialization (`Url.toString`) as the transport target — the
runtime never re-parses a fresh string to reconstruct it. Fails closed
(`Err`) on any non-`http(s)` scheme. There is no unmarked `String` default.

## `defaultRequestFromString`

```ipe
defaultRequestFromString : String -> Result Error HttpRequest
```

`defaultRequestFromString raw` — the MARKED parse-at-the-boundary helper
for a raw string target. It runs `Url.fromString` (the ONE parse of the
string) and then the same scheme narrowing, returning `Result` so a raw
string is an EXPLICIT parse boundary, never a silent stringly default. A
relative / scheme-less / non-`http(s)` string is a typed `Err`.

## `get`

```ipe
get : Url -> Task Error HttpResponse
```

`get url` — outbound GET. Takes an already-sealed typed `Url` (parsed once
at `Url.fromString`, the single SSRF parse boundary): a caller must
`Url.fromString` and handle the `Result` before calling, so a scheme-confused
or unparseable target can never reach the request. The runtime SSRF floor
(per-hop scheme allowlist + private-IP resolver) is unchanged — this typed
argument is defence-in-depth at the API boundary, not a replacement for it.

## `methodFromString`

```ipe
methodFromString : String -> Maybe HttpMethod
```

`methodFromString s` — the single typed parse boundary for inbound method
strings.  Returns `Just` the matching constructor for the seven standard
verbs (case-insensitive); returns `Nothing` for any unrecognised string.
Never silently defaults.

## `methodToString`

```ipe
methodToString : HttpMethod -> String
```

`methodToString m` — the canonical uppercase string for `m`
(e.g. `Get` → `"GET"`).  Use for logging or forwarding; the request
runtime converts `HttpMethod` to the reqwest `Method` internally.

## `parseQuery`

```ipe
parseQuery : String -> Result Error (Dict String String)
```

Decode a form-encoded query string into its key/value pairs.

A leading `?` is dropped and a repeated key keeps its first value. Returns
an `InvalidInput` error when any key or value holds a malformed
percent-escape or decodes to invalid UTF-8, and a `LimitExceeded` error when
the query carries more than 1024 pairs — there is no partial result.

## `post`

```ipe
post : Url -> String -> Task Error HttpResponse
```

`post url body` — outbound POST. Takes an already-sealed typed `Url` (see
`get`) and a request body. The runtime SSRF floor is unchanged.

## `withRedirects`

```ipe
withRedirects : RedirectPolicy -> HttpRequest -> HttpRequest
```

Set the redirect policy for a request.  `withRedirects NoRedirects`
prevents all redirects; `withRedirects (FollowRedirects n)` follows up to
`n` hops, and the hop past them fails the request with a `LimitExceeded`
error.

## `withTimeout`

```ipe
withTimeout : Duration -> HttpRequest -> HttpRequest
```

`withTimeout span req` — override the request timeout. Takes a typed
`Ipe.Duration` (e.g. `Duration.seconds 5`) so a caller names the unit at the
call site and a negative span is not representable; the raw milliseconds are
unwrapped into the transport DTO for the runtime, exactly as
`WebSocket.withTimeout` / `Cache.withTTL` do.

## `withUrl`

```ipe
withUrl : Url -> HttpRequest -> Result Error HttpRequest
```

`withUrl url req` — retarget an existing request to a typed `Url`. Like
`defaultRequest`, it re-narrows the scheme to `http`/`https` at the API
layer (fail-closed) and carries the single canonical serialization, so a
retarget cannot smuggle a non-`http(s)` scheme past the guard-off dev path.
